name: QRC MIDI
description: Sequence MIDI with a quantum reservoir — learn the notes of a file and generate a new arrangement as a fresh .mid.

output_files.name: state
output_files.description: Advanced reservoir state; reuse on a later call as job:<id>/state.

output_files.name: model
output_files.description: Pristine trained model for fan-out; reuse as job:<id>/model.

bpm.description: Tempo of the generated file in beats per minute. Note durations are preserved either way — this only sets the beat grid a DAW sees.
bpm.title: Bpm

loop.description: Treat the melody as looping material — the end flows back into the start. Learning only.
loop.title: Loop

quality.description: How hard to train when learning a fresh file (no `model`): instant skips training for a quick untrained shuffle; fast is quick and rough; complete is slow and tight.
quality.title: Quality

seed.description: Change for a different result, keep fixed to reproduce one. On a fresh file it also fixes the learned reservoir; when reusing a `model` it just varies the take, so you can fan out independent takes by changing it.
seed.title: Seed

variation.description: How freely the result departs from the learned order: low = tight and repetitive, high = loose and surprising.
variation.title: Variation

velocity.description: How hard every generated note is struck (1–127). One value for the whole file.
velocity.title: Velocity

description_md:
qrc-midi-v1 — sequence MIDI notes with a quantum reservoir.

A self-contained hybrid engine: one call trains a reservoir over the notes of a MIDI file, generates
a new ordering of them, and writes it back out as a `.mid`. Each note is a `pitch_duration` token
(e.g. "67_1.5") — the reservoir work is delegated to `qrc_core` (train/generate/state); this engine
only owns the MIDI codec (decode/encode) and the friendly parameter surface.

`quality: "instant"` skips training entirely (a quick untrained shuffle); the other levels train.

Three seed paths, chosen by which inputs arrive (no mode flag):
  - no `model`, quality != instant -> TRAIN on the file's notes, then generate. Emits a pristine
    `files.model` (reusable for fan-out) plus the advanced `files.state`.
  - no `model`, quality == instant -> untrained shuffle, emits `files.state` only.
  - `model` given -> reuse it (no `midi` needed): a pristine model (`job:<id>/model`) fans out an
    INDEPENDENT take (vary `seed`); an advanced state (`job:<id>/state`) CONTINUES that trajectory.
    The note vocabulary rides inside the artifact — nothing to re-upload.

Reservoir tuning (qubits, shots, epochs, windowing) lives in reservoir_tuning.py — a self-contained
"don't touch" file. Everything here is MIDI: the note codec and the request/response flow.

code_samples.source:
import requests
BASE = "https://api.mothquantum.com/v1"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_KEY"}

# 1. Learn a piece: train + first arrangement. Returns a .mid, a reusable model, and a state.
r = requests.post(
    f"{BASE}/generation/qrc-midi-v1/process",
    headers=HEADERS,
    files={"midi": open("piece.mid", "rb")},
    data={"length": 32, "quality": "moderate"},
)
job = r.json()["job_id"]   # ... poll GET {BASE}/status/{job} until "completed" ...
open("out.mid", "wb").write(requests.get(f"{BASE}/result/{job}", headers=HEADERS).content)

# 2. Fan out independent takes from the pristine model — no re-upload, no re-train.
for s in (1, 2, 3):
    requests.post(
        f"{BASE}/generation/qrc-midi-v1/process",
        headers=HEADERS,
        data={"model": f"job:{job}/model", "length": 32, "seed": s},
    )

# 3. Continue the phrase instead — reference the advanced state.
requests.post(
    f"{BASE}/generation/qrc-midi-v1/process",
    headers=HEADERS,
    data={"model": f"job:{job}/state", "length": 32},
)

curl -X POST https://api.mothquantum.com/v1/generation/qrc-midi-v1/process \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY" \
  -F midi=@piece.mid \
  -F length=32
# ... poll GET /v1/status/{job_id} until "completed", then:
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY" https://api.mothquantum.com/v1/result/{job_id} -o out.mid
